NCAAF
BYU @ UTAH • Sat 12:00pm
UTAH -5.5
-105
Spread
Picked: Nov 2 @ 1:54pm
Analysis
BYU’s 7-1 record is masked by big third-down plays, converting 54.7% (47 of 86), though they struggle elsewhere and have only converted 2 of 8 fourth downs. With a 10:00 AM kickoff at altitude, BYU’s third-down success could struggle. Against stronger teams, at UCF in Week 8, their defense gave up 39 points, and they barely defeated unranked Arizona State last week. Utah just beat Cincinnati 49-25 and previously shut down No. 18 Houston 21-13. Utah’s defense ranks fourth nationally at -0.14 EPA per play and owns a +41 first-down margin (182 vs 141) over BYU. Utah is also motivated to avenge last season’s 24-21 loss despite outgaining the Cougars 470-368. My model has the home team winning by 8 points.
NCAAF
BYU @ UTAH • Sat 12:00pm
Under 48.5
-110
Over/Under
Picked: Nov 3 @ 10:37am
Analysis
It's amazing how close this rivalry has been over the years. Dating back to 1997, 13 of 15 games in this series have been decided by a touchdown or less. And as for the total, each of the last seven meetings and 10 of the last 11 have gone under this number. Utah’s defense is giving up less than 16 points per game and BYU’s less than 19 PPG. This one does not feel like an offensive explosion by any means. Expect a one-possession game with the winner ending up in the low-20s. Utah 21, BYU 17.
NCAAF
VALPO @ DAY • Sat 12:00pm
DAY -8.5
-118
Spread
Picked: Nov 5 @ 8:48am
Analysis
Dayton has been on a tear since dropping their only game of the season a month ago and looks like a legit Top 25 team in the FCS. You have to tip your cap to the Beacon this season as Valpo at 4-4 has been extremely competitive. But this game is a measuring stick game that'll show the Beacon just how far they have left to go as a program.
NCAAF
UCLA @ MINN • Sat 12:00pm
UCLA -5
-111
Spread
Picked: Nov 5 @ 8:50am
Analysis
Run game and defense always travels and despite making the trek to Minneapolis, expect UCLA to pack both with them on the road. It has been their calling card all season long. And with each subsequent game, their backup QB just gains more experience and plays better and better. Bruins are well-coached and focused on the task at hand.
NCAAF
TEXAS @ MIZZOU • Sat 12:00pm
MIZZOU +3
-118
Spread
Picked: Nov 5 @ 8:52am
Analysis
Missouri will have both their tailbacks Jamal Roberts and Ahmad Hardy ready to go in this game in addition to a defense that can take advantage of a banged-up offensive line. I also believe the QB edge in this game goes to Austin Simmons. So for me, playing at home, with all of key head-to-head matchups in their favor, it's hard not to back Mizzou.

2026-27 MLB free agent tracker: Tarik Skubal, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Randy Arozarena and more available players
Who will land a new frontline ace or top slugger? Follow along as we keep track of all the moves
By
Kate Feldman
Nov 2, 2026
at
9:46 am ET
1 min read
Getty Images
Over the next several months leading up to the 2027 MLB season, hundreds of players will switch teams and sign new contracts -- and some will stay right were they were and sign new contracts. Hundreds of millions of dollars will change hands and new merchandise will flood the shops.
Tarik Skubal is the clear best player available on the market, an ace among aces who will play the entire season at age 30. Behind him are lesser but still solid options in guys like Jazz Chisholm Jr., Tyler Rogers, Randy Arozarena and Freddy Peralta.
Where will everyone land? CBS Sports will be keeping track of the top 50 free agents below.

College football schedule 2026: What to watch in Week 10, TV channels, streaming, Saturday kickoff times
The Week 10 schedule is loaded from top to bottom on Saturday, bringing us one of the most exciting slates in recent memory
By
Austin Nivison
Nov 6, 2026
at
9:35 am ET
5 min read
Getty Images
Welcome to one of the most highly anticipated weekends of college football in a long time. With seven ranked matchups on the board, it's going to be an exhilarating frenzy.
The day begins with the first-ever top-10 matchup in Holy War history as No. 9 BYU visits No. 3 Utah. The implications of that game are enormous, both in the Big 12 and for the College Football Playoff picture.
In the afternoon -- much to the chagrin of Lane Kiffin -- No. 14 LSU will host No. 5 Alabama. After the Crimson Tide were ranked shockingly high in the initial playoff rankings, the Tigers may have a point to prove in Death Valley. The loser will have three losses and playoff hopes on life support.
The day will be capped off by No. 1 Miami squaring off against No. 11 Notre Dame. Everyone circled this game before the season, and it hasn't lost any luster. The Hurricanes will be without Malachi Toney, but they can still do the job against South Bend. The Irish, on the other hand, really need to add a quality win to their resume.
Those three games alone are enough for a great Saturday, but there are still four more ranked matchups on the board. These are the types of days we dream about in the doldrums of the offseason.
To help you plan your day and prioritize the best matchups, we've compiled a handy viewer's guide.
The best games
No. 9 BYU at No. 3 Utah -- 12 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): This is in the conversation for the biggest Holy War game ever as the first top-10 matchup in the history of the rivalry. The Utes are undefeated and eyeing a first-round bye in the College Football Playoff. BYU is riding a three-game winning streak against its in-state rival, although the Cougars have underwhelmed in the two weeks since beating Notre Dame. Rice-Eccles Stadium will be a madhouse, and the Utes have never lost at home to BYU as an AP-ranked team. It's just a shame that this is a brunch kickoff locally, but that speaks to the strength of this slate.
No. 7 Texas at No. 18 Missouri -- 12 p.m. on ESPN, Fubo (try for free): This may not be a playoff eliminator because, theoretically, Texas has a shot to get in with three losses. That said, no one wants to be sitting on three losses in early November. It seems like the Longhorns have gotten back on track lately with consecutive wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State. Still, those have been costly wins. Texas' Wednesday night availability report featured a litany of key players listed as questionable. Can Missouri take advantage of that and beat Texas through the air with Austin Simmons hitting Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode early and often? That's the Tigers' clearest path to a victory.
No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU -- 3:30 p.m. on ABC, Fubo (try for free): First, let's take a moment of silence to mourn LSU missing out on a night game here. Despite all the talk about time slots, LSU has a great shot to win this game with the Sun in the sky. Sam Leavitt has been dealing of late, and Blake Baker's defense could give Keelon Russell some problems. Russell will be the key for Alabama. If the young quarterback can overcome earlier road struggles, he's capable of taking games over. Neither Kalen DeBoer nor Lane Kiffin can afford another loss, but one of them will be 6-3 on Sunday morning.
No. 23 Oregon at No. 12 Ohio State -- 3:30 p.m. on CBS, CBSSports.com, Paramount+ Premium: This game looks much different than what we expected coming into the season, but the stakes are still incredibly high. Oregon may have gained some confidence with a win over Northwestern, and Ohio State is coming off a disappointing loss in its first game without Julian Sayin. The x-factor in this matchup will be the development of Buckeyes freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who missed a few key throws against USC. If he takes a step forward from one start to the next, Ohio State should be in decent shape, especially with Jeremiah Smith on the outside.
No. 6 Kentucky at No. 13 Tennessee -- 6:15 p.m. on ESPN, Fubo (try for free): Kentucky has been one of the steadiest and most trustworthy teams in college football, but Tennessee has played extremely well at home. The chess match between Will Stein and Jim Knowles will be fascinating to watch, and the Neyland Stadium atmosphere for a "Dark Mode" game will give the Vols' defense an extra edge against the Wildcats. On the other side of the ball, Kentucky's secondary has questions, but sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre hasn't exactly carved anyone up just yet. Maybe that deficiency won't matter for the Cats.
No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame -- 7:30 p.m. on NBC, Fubo (try for free): This is one of the most highly anticipated games of the season, even without Malachi Toney on the field. The Heisman Trophy implications in this matchup will be off the charts with CJ Carr squaring off against Darian Mensah. The chances that one of those two produces a Heisman moment are extremely high. It's also a key data point for the College Football Playoff Selection Committee. Neither Notre Dame nor Miami faces a murderer's row this season, so it's a rare opportunity for each side to impress against a quality opponent.

The pair of top cruiserweights collide in London on Saturday night
By
Brent Brookhouse
Nov 6, 2026
at
1:26 pm ET
3 min read
Getty Images
Zuffa Boxing returns on Saturday with the upstart promotion's 12th numbered event. In the main event from Copper Box Arena in London, Chris Billam-Smith will take on Cheavon "C4" Clarke in an intriguing cruiserweight bout.
Both Billam-Smith and Clarke were successful in exciting Zuffa debuts, though in very different ways.
Billam-Smith, the former WBO cruiserweight champion, made his Zuffa debut against Ryan Rozicki in June. Billam-Smith looked tremendous throughout the fight, putting heaps of punishment on Rozicki, though Rozicki gained respect from the larger boxing world for showing an iron chin and loads of heart.
Sign up for Paramount+ and watch Zuffa Boxing 12 for no additional fee -- along with every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Eventually, Billam-Smith's attack was too much and Rozicki's corner stopped their fighter from taking any further punishment after seven rounds of action. It was a big statement for Billam-Smith, a well-known, talented fighter who decided to show he was willing to stand and trade in a style that gave Rozicki his only hope of victory.
Zuffa Boxing: Ranking the 10 best fights of the first 10 numbered events in 2026
Brent Brookhouse
While Billam-Smith's win was hard-fought but one-sided, Clarke had to battle back from significant adversity on the same card.
Clarke was facing Jack Massey when Massey scored two knockdowns in the fourth round of their bout. With things looking particularly dire, Clarke managed to turn things around, scoring his own knockdown in the seventh round and forcing the referee to stop the bout.
The win was Clarke's second since suffering back-to-back defeats to Leonardo Mosquea and Viddal Riley.
Zuffa Boxing 12 also features some other compelling fights with familiar names, including the return of Shane Mosley Jr. for the first time since his impressive win over Serhii Bohachuk when he faces Denzel Bentley in middleweight action, and a preliminary light heavyweight bout between Zach Parker and Umar Dzambekov.
Let's take a look at the complete card for Saturday night with the latest odds from DraftKings before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.
Zuffa Boxing 12 fight card, odds
Chris Billam-Smith -450 vs. Cheavon Clarke +320, cruiserweights

Where to watch Zuffa Boxing 12

Prelims begin at 12:15 p.m. ET
Main card begins at 2 p.m. ET
Watch live:  Paramount+ (subscribe now for as little as $8.99 per month)
Prediction
Billam-Smith has been to the top of the sport, holding a legitimate world championship and making multiple successful defenses. He's not a perfect boxer, but he's a skilled one who has shown that he can box or slug when the fight calls for it. Billam-Smith knows that standing and trading gives Clarke his best (and maybe only) path to victory, but that didn't stop Billam-Smith from doing the same against Rozicki.
Still, the reality is that Clarke needs Billam-Smith to make some bad decisions and leave big openings for him to win. Clarke has power and he did pick himself up off the canvas twice in his most recent win, but Billam-Smith is a far better fighter than Massey. Billam-Smith is also considerably better than Mosquea and Riley, both of whom beat Clarke on the scorecards.
It's easy to see Billam-Smith winning almost any style of fight with Clarke, but hard to see Clarke winning any way other than connecting with one big punch. I see a cautious start for Billam-Smith before he turns up the heat and ges a late stoppage. Pick: Chris Billam-Smith via TKO9

A closer look at the top games on tap Saturday as college football Week 10 takes center stage

This is the weekend we've all been waiting for this season. Preorder your food now and claim the best seat on the couch because you'll be glued to the television all day Saturday.
There are seven games featuring top-25 vs. top-25 teams on Saturday. All of them have significant College Football Playoff implications.
Start your day off with the Holy War in Utah when No. 9 BYU takes on No. 3 Utah (noon ET). The Utes are currently in the driver's seat in the Big 12, but BYU could shake up the race with a win over its in-state rival. How this game shakes out could have a big impact on how many bids the Big 12 secures this season.
It's a stacked weekend slate for the SEC. It starts with No. 7 Texas at No. 18 Missouri, with each a two-loss team hoping to stay in the race. No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU could be a playoff eliminator, especially for the Tigers. Alabama may have enough wiggle room to survive a loss and still get in at 9-3, though Kalen DeBoer would surely prefer not to have to test that theory. LSU coach Lane Kiffin is still trying for his first career win over Alabama.
No. 10 Ole Miss could all but clinch a spot in the field if it can again beat a No. 2 Georgia program it knocked out of last year's playoff. Unfortunately for the Rebels, they'll be without star running back Kewan Lacy, who had two touchdowns against the Bulldogs in the Sugar Bowl.
In Knoxville, can Will Stein and No. 6 Kentucky Wildcats keep the best story in college football going with a road win over No. 13 Tennessee?
One of the more intriguing games happens in Columbus between No. 23 Oregon and No. 12 Ohio State. Things haven't gone according to plan for either of the preseason's top two teams in the country. Both are down their star quarterback and have little to no margin for error this season. The Buckeyes are the first team out of the playoff field and will need to beat the Ducks to prove to the selection committee they are still one of the nation's best teams, even without Julian Sayin. Oregon is a long shot to make the playoff and could not only spoil OSU's hopes but also increase the odds the Big Ten gets only two playoff teams.
Finish your night off with No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame. The game may have lost a little juice without star receiver Malachi Toney, but the stakes are still quite high for the Fighting Irish. A loss in South Bend on Saturday night could doom Notre Dame to another missed playoff appearance.

articles.text:

section: | slug: nfl-trade-deadline-4-trade-options-steelers-super-bowl-contender | sport: football | route: article_single.us |

NFL Trade Deadline: 4 mock trades that would make Steelers a true Super Bowl contender
Pittsburgh needs to make the most of its 6-2 start while giving Aaron Rodgers a real chance to win big in his final season
By
Bryan DeArdo
Nov 6, 2026
at
10:30 am ET
4 min read
Getty Images
After a 2-2 start, the Pittsburgh Steelers head into their bye week with a 6-2 record and sole possession of first place in the AFC North division.
More impressive than Pittsburgh's record is how the Steelers have gotten here. The Steelers' defense is currently third in the NFL in points allowed (they haven't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters). The offensive line is coming into its own. Jaylen Warren is having a breakout season (and his backup, Rico Dowdle, is making an impact as well). Aaron Rodgers still has his legendary throwing touch.
Pittsburgh might already have all the pieces it needs to end its nine-year drought without a playoff win. But if they really want to give themselves a shot at getting to the Super Bowl, the Steelers should try to acquire a receiver before the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
The Steelers have gotten considerable production from rookie Germie Bernard, and they continue to get production in the passing game from tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth. Warren and Dowdle have helped, too. Those players have helped mask the issue, but eventually, the Steelers' lack of weaponry at receiver will be exposed — most likely in the playoffs.
Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman's injuries, plus  DK Metcalf's struggles, have once again put the Steelers in the market for a receiver. Here are four potential trades the Steelers should try to make at the deadline.
Trade 1
Steelers receive: Ladd McConkey, 2027 fifth-round pick
Chargers receive: Roman Wilson, 2027 second-round pick
It's possible that the Steelers wouldn't have to part with Wilson in this scenario, but if the Chargers want a replacement for McConkey, it would likely be Wilson, who had success at Michigan with Jim Harbaugh.
The Chargers also probably don't want to part with McConkey, a former 1,000-yard receiver who is still playing on his rookie contract. However, getting another receiver — in addition to a second-round pick — could be enough for the Chargers to move McConkey.
Pittsburgh surely doesn't want to part with a second-round pick. With Rodgers retiring, the Steelers will continue their pursuit to find a long-term quarterback in 2027 and will want as many draft picks as possible to improve their odds at finding that player in next year's draft. That's where the fifth-round pick comes into play, as it somewhat softens the blow of losing a second-rounder.
McConkey's arrival will help soften the blow, too. He's a young, talented receiver who could make an immediate impact in Pittsburgh's offense. He's also affordable and would still be under contract for the 2027 season.
Trade 2
Steelers receive: Brian Thomas Jr., 2027 fifth-round pick
Jaguars receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick
A former Pro Bowler, Thomas has spent most of the 2026 season languishing on the Jaguars' bench. He would benefit from a fresh start, and the Jaguars may decide to give it to him ahead of the trade deadline in exchange for a high draft pick.
This is a good trade for the Steelers on multiple fronts. In Thomas, they'd be getting a 6-foot-2, 209-pound playmaker that would help open things up for Metcalf and give Rodgers another big red zone target. The Steelers wouldn't have to part with Wilson.
The big question is whether the Jaguars would trade Thomas to a team they will face later this year (Jacksonville will host Pittsburgh in Week 14) and possibly again in the playoffs. They might be compelled to do so if the compensation is right.
Trade 3
Steelers receive: Jerry Jeudy
Browns receive: 2027 fourth-round pick
The biggest challenge here would be the Browns' likely preference to trade Jeudy to a non-divisional team. However, the Browns did show last year (when they traded Joe Flacco to Cincinnati) that they will make an in-season trade with a division rival. It also helps that the Steelers and Browns are done playing each other this season barring a playoff matchup.
Like Thomas, Jeudy is a former Pro Bowler who needs a change of scenery. He's just two years removed from catching 90 passes for 1,229 yards, which he did on a Browns team that won just three games.
Trade 4
Steelers receive: Josh Downs
Colts receive: 2027 third-round pick
This is a pretty clean trade. The Steelers strengthen their receiving corps by adding Downs, and the Colts get another decently high draft pick for their rebuild. It's a win-win for both teams.
There are some possible issues, however, starting with the Steelers possibly being in a bidding war for Downs, who is good but probably isn't worth more than a third-round pick. However, it only takes one team to drive up the price.
Indianapolis' expectations in a trade for Downs should be tempered because of the fact that he is slated to enter free agency after the season. He'd essentially be a rental for whoever gets him.
From Pittsburgh's perspective, this is a good trade despite having to give up a third-round pick. The Steelers wouldn't have to part with any of their receivers and would be getting a proven slot receiver who has 228 career receptions.

Is Drew Mestemaker really QB1? A troubling trend and lessons from Caleb Williams, Trevor Lawrence
The Oklahoma State QB has become a popular QB1 choice, but his mistakes under pressure offer a warning – and some fascinating historical comparisons.
By
Ryan Wilson
Nov 6, 2026
at
3:16 pm ET
6 min read
Getty Images
Caleb Williams. Trevor Lawrence. Drew Mestemaker.
Two former No. 1 overall picks and probably the hottest name in the 2027 NFL Draft all share a troubling distinction: Over the last decade-plus, only Williams and Lawrence had higher turnover-worthy-play rates under pressure in their final college seasons than Mestemaker has this year.
But there's a catch. For Williams and Lawrence, those numbers were one-year blips after considerably better performances earlier in their college careers. For Mestemaker, the mistakes have followed him from North Texas to Oklahoma State … and they've gotten worse.
None of that means Mestemaker can't be the first quarterback selected in the 2027 NFL Draft. He's put himself squarely in the QB1 conversation, and for good reason. I have Miami's Darian Mensah just ahead of him, but there's a whole lot to like about Mestemaker's game.
NFL teams will also have to answer an important question before investing a high first-round pick in him: What happens when defenses take away the easy throws and force him to make decisions under pressure?
Why Mestemaker belongs in the QB1 conversation
There's plenty to like about the Oklahoma State quarterback, who spent last season at North Texas. For starters, Mestemaker looks the part. He has a strong arm, throws with anticipation and will get through his reads. He's comfortable attacking all three levels, manipulates defenders with his eyes and has the patience to stand in the pocket, reset his feet and deliver fastballs into tight windows.
Just watched Drew Mestemaker's throws vs. UCF, and he just keeps getting better. BTW, if Arch Manning had Mestemaker's tape, he'd be the consensus QB1, probably by a wide margin.
Wrote about Mestemaker after he beat Oregon and he's playing better now. https://t.co/MPhvkXpD60— ryan wilson (@ryanwilsonCBS) October 11, 2026
He has plenty of NFL-caliber throws on tape, especially on intermediate routes where he has to throw receivers open. It's easy to see why he's become a popular QB1 choice. But there are also stretches where he tries to do too much, and that's where the evaluation gets more complicated.
The concern isn't just this season
Through Week 9 of 2026, Mestemaker has seven turnover-worthy plays on 54 dropbacks when he was pressured, according to PFF. That's a 13.0% rate, more than double the 5.8% median for the first-round quarterbacks in our historical comparison.
(A turnover-worthy play isn't just an interception. It can be a dangerous throw that a defender drops or another mistake that puts the football at risk. And while the number itself doesn't tell us everything, it helps identify decisions that might otherwise get lost in the box score.)
Williams and Lawrence were the only first-rounders we looked at with higher rates in their final college seasons, but both had been considerably better the previous year. Williams went from 0.9% in 2022 to 15.3% in 2023, while Lawrence jumped from 1.6% in 2019 to 13.2% in 2020.

Look at Williams and Lawrence now. Both had bumpy starts to their NFL careers, and both are now two of the NFL's best quarterbacks. It's a pretty good reminder that A.) landing in the right situation is probably the most important factor in a young QB's development, and B.) troubling college numbers don't mean you're destined to fail at the next level.
Mestemaker's struggles have followed him from North Texas to Oklahoma State. His turnover-worthy-play rate was 8.3% under pressure in 2025 before climbing to 13% so far this season. Over that span, he's put the ball in harm's way 13 times in 126 such situations. That's a 10.3% rate, and it's something NFL evaluators will have to consider.
Of course, there's recent precedent for NFL teams looking past troubling numbers. I wrote last November about Ty Simpson's historically poor deep-ball accuracy, and we later learned just how much injuries had affected his play. The Rams still took him 13th overall in April, betting on everything else he did well.
Here's what makes it even more interesting: Mestemaker has gotten much better at avoiding sacks, but he's also making more dangerous throws. Last season, he was sacked on roughly 21% of plays when pressured. That number is down to 11% this year, but while he's taking fewer sacks, he's also averaging a full yard less per pass attempt in those situations (5.6 to 4.5).
The tape provides more clues. Mestemaker generally shows good footwork and accuracy when he has time, and he's capable of working beyond his first read. But there are also moments when he forces throws into coverage instead of taking the easier completion underneath, or when his accuracy suffers because he doesn't get his feet set.
These aren't all necessarily mistakes caused by pressure, but they point to a similar concern: knowing when to challenge a defense and when to take what it's giving you.

NFL Week 9 underrated games: An international game, two AFC vs. NFC showdowns to add to your watch list
A look at three games you should keep an eye on this week
By
Shanna McCarriston
Nov 6, 2026
at
10:00 am ET
3 min read
Todd Kirkland/Getty Images
Week 9 of 2026 is an exciting one. The trade deadline is right around the corner, and teams have until Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET to sell or add to their team.
There have already been moves made, and rumors are swirling about multiple players across the league. This will be a big week for teams to watch players they're interested in to determine if they want to make a move.
There are some obvious big games this week, but there are also some underrated games you should be tuning into. Here is a look at three games that should be on your radar:
Bengals vs. Falcons
Sunday, Nov. 8 at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
Who doesn't love to wake up and immediately watch football? The international game this week is in Spain, which already adds an exciting extra element to the matchup.
These two teams, specifically their quarterbacks, are coming off wildly different games. Last week, Falcons QB Michael Penix had a career-high four interceptions in their 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers. Bengals QB Joe Burrow threw five touchdown passes and ran in the overtime game-winner in their 43-36 battle against the Titans.
The matchup I'm interested in is the Falcons' defense against the Bengals' passing game, specifically wide receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase. Higgins is second in yards per game (103.7), while Chase is 16th in the league (70.3), making them a duo very difficult for secondaries to stop. The Bengals lead the NFL in passing yards per game (288.4), and the Falcons defense is in the middle of the pack in passing yards allowed (223.4).
The Bengals come in at 5-2, while the Falcons are 3-5 but have shown real flashes of strong play. Coming off two vastly different games, plus international travel, this game could surprise people.
Broncos vs. Panthers
Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
This one isn't a divisional, or even conference, matchup, so it will go under the radar more than some of the direct intraconference showdowns, but I think it will be one of the best games of the week.
The Broncos are riding high after a huge divisional win over the Chiefs, in a game that came down to the final play. They now lead the AFC West and are looking to keep that status and extend their four-game win streak.
In their way are the Panthers, who should come out aggressive, looking to snap a two-game losing streak. Despite being 3-4, the Panthers lead the NFC South in a battle of rebuilding teams, with up-and-down performances.
Carolina is ninth in yards per game (363.7), while the Broncos defense has allowed the eighth-most yards per game (355.3), creating an interesting matchup. Another intriguing element of the game goes back to the trade deadline. The Broncos have been tied heavily to running back Jonathan Taylor, who is a top trade candidate.
Buccaneers vs. Bears
Sunday, Nov. 8 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC (Stream: fubo, try for free)
Both teams are coming off wins, but in very different fashions. The Bucs defeated the Falcons 16-0 without completing a single pass. The run game thrived in the rainy game, with Bucky Irving finishing with 170 yards and Kenneth Gainwell rushing for 140 yards.
The Bears won their last three, including a big win in primetime last week against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks. Chicago is second in the NFC North in a tight race with the Vikings, who are 6-1.
A battle between Bucs QB Baker Mayfield and Bears QB Caleb Williams has big potential, and with both teams in tight divisional races and sitting in second place in their respective divisions, both teams have playoff aspirations. Chicago is the better team, more likely to go further in the postseason, but with Tampa settling back in with Mayfield's return, they could improve down the stretch.
Another player to watch during the game is defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who will be playing his second game with the Bears after a blockbuster trade with the Titans.

2026 NFL trade deadline: One realistic, one pipe dream trade scenario for every playoff contender
What does each contender need to put them over the top?
By
JP Acosta
Nov 6, 2026
at
6:00 am ET
23 min read
Stephen Maturen/Getty Images
The NFL trade deadline is less than a week away, and every team is in position to either put themselves over the top in hopes of a playoff push, or to completely reset their franchise and move on to NFL Draft season.
We've already seen big names like LG Quenton Nelson and DTs DeForest Buckner and Jeffrey Simmons getting dealt before the deadline. And I get the feeling that more big names will be on the move once we get to November 10.
For every team in the current playoff picture, we'll break down one realistic trade and one pipe dream trade they can make to put themselves over the top, in addition to a few interesting ones outside of the playoff mix.
AFC
1 . Buffalo Bills
Pipe Dream Trade: Jessie Bates, S, Atlanta Falcons
Realistic Trade: Amani Hooker, S, Tennessee Titans
The Bills have gotten more than enough from their defensive front, a unit that I thought would come along slowly in the beginning of the season. EDGE Greg Rousseau is playing at a DPOY-caliber level, and the emergence of DT Deone Walker has helped their defensive line gain some teeth. However, the Bills have given up the fifth-most completions of 20+ yards in the NFL this season and lack impact play from their secondary.
Cornerback is a spot where they could improve, but they have a lot of faith in rookie CB Davison Igbinosun opposite Christian Benford. However, the safety spot opposite Cole Bishop could use some improvement. While most people will point to Arizona Cardinals' safety Budda Baker as the top target, he and Bishop's skillsets overlap.
Bates is entering the final year of his contract with the Falcons, and he has been an impact player when the ball is in the air and when separating the ball from the player (three PBUs, one INT and three forced fumbles in 2026). Bates is the perfect complement to Bishop and could help tilt the scales back in the Bills' favor.
Hooker makes a lot of sense as a realistic target for the Bills. There's some freedom in his contract as he enters the final two years of his 2025 deal, but he's a reliable post safety who can complement Bishop's skills closer to the line of scrimmage.
2. Denver Broncos
Pipe Dream Trade: RB Jonathan Taylor, Indianapolis Colts
Realistic Trade: TE Dallas Goedert, Philadelphia Eagles
I wouldn't be surprised if the Broncos ultimately stand pat at the deadline, after all the rumors and whispers that they're looking for something big. With the emergence of RB Jonah Coleman in this offense, the Denver running game has found some new life to go along with the mandatory second-half Bo Nix resurgence.
However, if the Broncos were looking to make a big swing, it would obviously be for Colts' RB Jonathan Taylor. While Coleman has been very good, the explosiveness Taylor would bring makes a pedestrian Broncos offense more dangerous from anywhere on the field (since 2023, Taylor has 78 explosive runs, 5th-most in the NFL). This season, Denver is 26th in Explosive Play Rate, behind teams like the Philadelphia Eagles and the Tennessee Titans, and offense gets really hard when you can't generate explosives. Taylor is not only a big-play machine but would also loosen some of the constraints on the Denver offense as they try to make the Super Bowl.
Now, for a realistic trade scenario, I do think the Broncos look at other positions. I doubt they'd be able to get him from within the division, but LB Daiyan Henley could really give the Broncos' defense a nitro boost. However, I'm eyeing Eagles' TE Dallas Goedert as a realistic trade target.
The Broncos have gotten next to nothing out of their tight end group this year (second-lowest receiving yards to TEs this season, per TruMedia). Goedert is entering the final year of his contract with the Eagles. He would give the Broncos a reliable player down the seams and a competitive blocker who wouldn't be an obvious tell when he's on the field.
3. Pittsburgh Steelers
Pipe Dream Trade: WR Josh Downs, Indianapolis Colts
Realistic Trade: CB Amik Robertson, Washington Commanders
The Steelers have surprisingly found themselves at the top of the AFC North behind an offense that's gone fully into bullyball, but at the deadline I think adding a receiver with some separation skills could really give the Pittsburgh passing offense some juice. The Steelers have struggled this season throwing against man coverage, ranking 25th in EPA per play and 30th in Success Rate on all dropbacks against man coverage.  DK Metcalf hasn't inspired much confidence in the receiver room, and despite the emergence of rookie Germie Bernard, the room overall doesn't have much teeth.
Enter Josh Downs, who is the exact receiver this version of the Steelers needs. Since 2023, among all players with 175 total targets, Downs is 13th in the NFL in percentage of receptions  (80.4%) against man coverage that go for first downs or touchdowns. While he's more of a slot receiver, he's a guy who can win with crafty route running and acceleration in and out of breaks. QB Aaron Rodgers loves throwing sight adjustments and option slants to receivers when he sees the number count in his favor, but those haven't worked with Metcalf. Downs can win on those and give the Steelers an easy button in their passing game.
